evidence_works.work: Dobui 2020, Modelisation des traits laryngaux du diasysteme chinanteque (otomangue central) (Verbum XLII 2(1): 22 pp., HAL hal-04043742)
evidence_works.note: Diasystem-level modelling built from existing descriptions, not fieldwork; the data come mainly from Rensch (1968), and for 18 localities, Petlapa among them, they were 'compilees aussi par Rensch de sources de seconde main'. Adds three family-level points to the entry: (a) every Chinantec variety has three to five basic tones plus melodic tones (p. 7), consistent with the entry's five levels plus four contours; (b) final glottal frication CVh is recorded, on Rensch's data, in I-Sochiapan and in the variety-IV localities Lalana, Lacova, Petlapa, Teotalcingo, Rio Chiquito and La Alicia, and is reanalysed, following Herrera (2000), as ballisticity, a syllable-level laryngeal contrast (p. 9); fn. 8 (p. 11) counts 'toutes les localites de la variete IV' among the localities with ballisticity; (c) ballisticity 'a ete souvent considere comme lie a l'accent' (p. 14) but Dobui argues it 'n'est pas qu'une question d'accent' (p. 15), citing Mugele (1984) on IV-Lalana for its phonetics (p. 11). The entry's first-hand source (Nakamoto 2026, Cuadro B.1, p. 512) labels three tones of Arroyo Blanco Petlapa with 'aspiracion final (V)' -- /3/ 'medio nivel', /32/ 'bajo descendente' and /42/ 'medio descendente' -- the '(V)' being the table's symbol for the short modal-vowel syllable type (columns V: VˀV V:ˀ V Vˀ); its inventory is '9 tonos, cantidad vocalica binaria, y tres tipos de fonacion (modal, glotalizacion final, y glotalizacion medial)', 28 patterns (p. 509), with no ballistic category, and for Lalana the same author treats final aspiration as 'una caracteristica fonetica del tono' and not a ballistic-syllable feature as in Mugele (1982) (p. 78). So Dobui's Petlapa point is a secondhand family-level classification that the entry cites for context, not for coding.

tn.quote: 0.2. L’alladian est une langue à tons. Chaque mot comporte dans sa prononciation un contour mélodique appelé schème tonal ... 0.3. Selon moi, il y a quatre tonèmes en alladian ... Il s’agit de trois tons ponctuels (haut, moyen et bas) et un ton modulé haut-bas ... tout porte à croire que le ton modulé moyen-bas est une variante contextuelle du ton moyen. ... 0.4. En résumé, on peut admettre un système intégré de quatre tonèmes en alladian.
tn.translation: 0.2. Alladian is a tone language. Every word carries in its pronunciation a melodic contour called a tonal scheme ... 0.3. In my view there are four tonemes in Alladian ... These are three level tones (high, mid and low) and one high-low contour tone ... everything suggests that the mid-low contour tone is a contextual variant of the mid tone. ... 0.4. In summary, one may posit an integrated system of four tonemes in Alladian.
tn.cite: Somé, Joachim. 1998. L'orthographe pratique de l'alladian. Deuxième partie: une méthode de notation sélective des tons. Abidjan, février 1998. 34 pp.
tn.note: Four tonemes: level H, M, L plus falling HL; a mid-low fall is a word-final variant of mid. Verb conjugations use low/high tonal morphemes; no floating lexical tones in nominals. Nothing on stress. Checked against the source (tone consistency check round 3, 2026-09-24): tone-bearing unit unstated -> syllable (§0.5 p.7 and §1.2.2 p.11 …).

5327.prule: Stress is not lexically contrastive but rhythmic: each phonological word contains one non-iterative trochaic foot with an obligatorily heavy (branching) nucleus built on the root (CVV monosyllabic roots; disyllabic roots stressed on their first syllable, CVXCV), with proclitics and enclitics unstressed.
5327.quote: The basic pattern for stress in the word is to build a binary trochaic foot with a heavy nucleus. ... Unlike Zapotec stress, which is not lexically contrastive but is instead rhythmical in function, Spanish stress is phonemic (lexically contrastive).
5327.loc: p.68 (sec. 3.3, Fig. 3.3 'Zapotec stress: Non-iterative trochaic foot with obligatorily branching nucleus') and p.71

tn.quote: Zapotec should be analyzed as a "pitch accent language" and not as a canonical "tone language." ... Zapotec pitch accents are based in a two-tone contrast that specifies high tone and low tone. There is also the unmarked case of the mid level to produce a five-way contrast in monosyllabic words. ... Lachixío and Asunción Zapotec pitch accent systems are very similar. Each contains an inventory that includes a high accent, low accent, and a combination of low and high that produces a rising accent, a combination of high and low that produces a falling accent ...
